concerns: The proposed national preference is weak because both “khalayak” and “audiens” are understood and used in both Indonesian and Malaysian Malay for this sense.
response.cue_rationale: “Audience” clearly denotes people listening to or watching a speaker or performance, matching both answers.
material_concerns: The pairing may mislead learners into treating the forms as country-exclusive or strongly preferred by country.

preference_risk.rationale: Both proposed forms are plausibly ordinary in both varieties for the same audience sense.

response.rationale: Both answers fit the same audience sense, but the contrast is not reliably national: Indonesian also uses “audiens,” while Malaysian Malay can use “khalayak.”
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Audiens” is ordinary in Indonesian and “khalayak” is also available in Malaysian Malay, so ordinary usage could defeat the proposed preference contrast.
